entities.label: Sketchpad
entities.blurb: Ivan Sutherland's 1963 light-pen drawing program that invented interactive computer graphics in a single PhD thesis.

entities.label: David C. Evans
entities.blurb: Built the University of Utah graphics program that trained a generation, then co-founded Evans & Sutherland.

entities.label: AMD
entities.blurb: The CPU maker that bought ATI and later donated Mantle, reshaping the entire modern graphics API landscape.

entities.label: STB Systems
entities.blurb: The Texas board maker whose acquisition turned 3dfx's card-making partners into enemies overnight.

entities.label: Kurt Akeley
entities.blurb: SGI co-founder who architected RealityEngine and co-wrote the OpenGL specification.

entities.label: IRIS GL
entities.blurb: SGI's proprietary workstation graphics API whose cleaned-up open descendant became OpenGL.

entities.label: ATI Technologies
entities.blurb: The Toronto chipmaker that outlived 3dfx to become NVIDIA's last standing rival before AMD absorbed it.

entities.label: VGA
entities.blurb: IBM's 1987 display standard whose 640x480 fallback mode PCs still boot into decades later.

entities.label: PHIGS
entities.blurb: The ISO-blessed retained-mode 3D standard that OpenGL's immediate-mode pragmatism steamrolled.

entities.label: S3 Graphics

milestones.what: S3TC texture compression licensed into DirectX 6
graphics unit sold into a VIA joint venture

entities.blurb: A 2D-era giant that lost the 3D race but whose S3TC compression outlived it inside every GPU.

entities.label: OpenGL

milestones.what: stewardship passes from the ARB to Khronos

entities.blurb: The cross-platform 3D API that carried real-time graphics from SGI workstations to every desktop and, via ES, every phone.

entities.label: OpenGL ARB
entities.blurb: The industry review board that governed OpenGL by committee for fourteen contentious years.

entities.label: RealityEngine
entities.blurb: SGI's million-dollar textured-graphics monster, the machine every 90s VR lab dreamed of owning.

entities.label: Chris Malachowsky
entities.blurb: Sun GX graphics co-inventor who brought silicon engineering muscle to NVIDIA's founding trio.

entities.label: Curtis Priem
entities.blurb: Architect of Sun's GX graphics who designed NVIDIA's early chip architectures as founding CTO.

entities.label: Gary Tarolli
entities.blurb: SGI graphics veteran who co-founded 3dfx as CTO and architected the Voodoo line.

entities.label: DirectX / Direct3D

milestones.what: Direct3D debuts from the RenderMorphics acquisition

entities.blurb: Microsoft's game-platform weapon that fought OpenGL for a decade and won the Windows desktop.

entities.label: Glide
entities.blurb: 3dfx's slim proprietary API, briefly the fast path every PC game targeted before open standards caught up.

entities.label: Voodoo Graphics
entities.blurb: The add-in card that made PC gamers see texture-filtered 3D for the first time and never look back.

entities.label: Fahrenheit
entities.blurb: The doomed Microsoft-SGI treaty to unify Direct3D and OpenGL, which mostly bought Microsoft time while SGI's API leadership drained away.

entities.label: RIVA 128
entities.blurb: The Direct3D-first chip that saved a nearly broke NVIDIA and put it on the map against 3dfx.

entities.label: GeForce 256
entities.blurb: Marketed as the world's first GPU, it pulled transform and lighting onto the chip and named an entire category.

entities.label: Radeon
entities.blurb: ATI's GPU brand, still AMD's answer to GeForce a quarter century on.

entities.label: OpenGL ES
entities.blurb: The trimmed-down OpenGL for embedded devices that ended up rendering every smartphone screen on Earth.

entities.label: CUDA

milestones.what: AlexNet trains on two GeForce GTX 580s, igniting deep learning

entities.blurb: NVIDIA's bet that gamers' chips could do general compute, which accidentally became the substrate of modern AI.

entities.label: Vladimir Vukicevic
entities.blurb: The Mozilla engineer who prototyped Canvas 3D into WebGL, then conceived WebVR — twice opening browsers to new hardware.

entities.label: Ricardo Cabello (mr.doob)
entities.blurb: The demoscene coder known as mr.doob who single-handedly bootstrapped three.js and web 3D culture.

entities.label: Brandon Jones
entities.blurb: The Google engineer who brought WebVR to Chrome and became a principal editor of the WebXR spec.

entities.label: WebGL

milestones.what: WebGL 1.0 ships in Firefox 4 and Chrome

entities.blurb: The API that put a real GPU behind every browser tab, making 3D on the web a default rather than a plugin.

entities.label: Mantle
entities.blurb: AMD's short-lived low-overhead API whose real legacy was being donated as the foundation of Vulkan.

entities.label: Metal

milestones.what: Apple deprecates OpenGL in Metal's favor

entities.blurb: Apple's low-overhead GPU API, the walled-garden answer to Vulkan and the flavor of its WebGPU proposal.

entities.label: WebVR

milestones.what: WebVR 1.0 proposal from Mozilla and Google teams

entities.blurb: The experimental API that plugged VR headsets into browsers and proved the immersive web was possible.

entities.label: Vulkan
entities.blurb: Khronos's explicit, cross-platform successor to OpenGL, built from the bones of AMD's Mantle.

entities.label: WebGPU
entities.blurb: The browser's next GPU interface, abstracting Vulkan, Metal, and D3D12 and bringing compute shaders to the web.

entities.label: WebXR
entities.blurb: WebVR's successor, folding AR and VR into a single W3C standard for immersive browsers.
